draft.title: Transcription
card: Transcription is the first step in making a protein from a gene. It copies the gene's DNA message into RNA. In eukaryotic cells it happens in the nucleus.
The enzyme RNA polymerase binds to the start of the gene. It unwinds the DNA and reads one strand, called the template strand.
RNA polymerase adds RNA nucleotides that pair with the template strand: A pairs with U, T with A, C with G and G with C. This builds a single strand of RNA.
The new strand is pre-mRNA. Its base sequence matches the other DNA strand, except that it has uracil in place of thymine. The DNA itself is not changed.
draft.remember: RNA polymerase reads the template strand and builds pre-mRNA with matching bases.

a.q: What does RNA polymerase do during transcription?
opts: Builds pre-mRNA by pairing bases to the template strand
Joins amino acids together to build a polypeptide
Copies both DNA strands to make new double-stranded DNA
Removes the template strand from the nucleus
a.why: RNA polymerase adds RNA nucleotides that pair with the template strand, making pre-mRNA. Joining amino acids is a different step, which happens later, and the DNA is not copied or removed.
a.clue: The enzyme's name tells you what it builds.

b.q: A section of template strand reads TACGGA. Which pre-mRNA sequence is made from it?
opts: AUGCCU
ATGCCT
AUGGCU
UACGGA
b.why: Each template base pairs with an RNA base: T with A, A with U, C with G, G with C, G with C, A with U. This gives AUGCCU. ATGCCT is wrong because RNA has uracil, not thymine. UACGGA copies the template instead of pairing with it.
b.clue: Pair each base, and remember RNA has no thymine.

a.best: Builds pre-mRNA by pairing bases to the template strand

problems.detail: "Builds pre-mRNA with matching bases" is ambiguous. The pre-mRNA pairs with (is complementary to) the template strand and matches the other strand. A student could read "matching" as the same bases as the template, which is the UACGGA error.
The why says "the DNA is not copied", but the card says transcription "copies the gene's DNA message into RNA". It should say the DNA is not copied into new DNA.
